* [[American occupation of Iraq|Occupation of Iraq]]: Protests in the city of [[Amarah]] because of [[unemployment]] occur. Police officers and soldiers open fire on demonstrators. Five or six are killed and one or eleven wounded.<ref name="autogenerated2004b">{{cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/01/11/sprj.nirq.main/index.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218042726/http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/01/11/sprj.nirq.main/index.html |archive-date=2008-12-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* In publicity for a new book for which former U.S. [[United States Secretary of the Treasury|Treasury Secretary]] [[Paul O'Neill (businessman)|Paul O'Neill]] is the primary source, ''[[60 Minutes]]'' reveals O'Neill's claims that the [[George W. Bush|Bush]] administration was making plans for an [[2003 invasion of Iraq|invasion of Iraq]] within days of Bush's [[inauguration]]. Bush officials note that [[regime change]] in Iraq had been official U.S. policy since 1998, three years before Bush took office.  O'Neill, fired for his opposition to [[Jobs and Growth Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003|tax cuts]], also characterized Bush as so disengaged in [[United States Cabinet|cabinet meetings]] that he "was like a blind man in a roomful of deaf people". On the positive side, O'Neill also described Bush as such a good listener that he (O'Neill) was able to give a non-stop monologue for nearly an hour in a one-on-one meeting.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/stories/2004/01/09/60minutes/main592330.shtml |title=Bush Sought 'Way' To Invade Iraq? |publisher=CBS News |date= |accessdate=2015-10-25}}</ref>
* ''[[SCO v. IBM]]'': [[SCO Group]] claims that it has "low-level talks" with [[Google]] about a possible license agreement related to [[Linux]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/markets/bonds/newswire/2004/01/09/rtr1205268.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-12-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070806200350/http://www.forbes.com/markets/bonds/newswire/2004/01/09/rtr1205268.html |archive-date=2007-08-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[Iraq and weapons of mass destruction]]: On January 9, 2004, [[Military of Denmark|Danish troops]] discovered decade-old [[Mortar (weapon)|mortar]] rounds containing suspicious liquid buried in Southern [[Iraq]]. Initial tests now indicate that the rounds contain the banned [[Chemical warfare|chemical weapon]] [[blister gas]].  Final tests should be available in two days.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/01/10/sprj.irq.chemicals/index.html |title=Suspicious shells found in southern Iraq - Jan. 11, 2004 |publisher=CNN.com |date=2004-01-11 |accessdate=2015-10-25}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=58 mins ago |url=http://story.news.yahoo.com/news?tmpl=story&cid=564&ncid=564&e=3&u=/nm/20040110/ts_nm/iraq_chemicals_dc_5 |title=Yahoo News - Latest News & Headlines |publisher=Story.news.yahoo.com |date=2011-04-20 |accessdate=2015-10-25}}</ref>
* A speed boat carrying [[illegal immigrants]] from [[Albania]], bound for Italy broke down and capsized. There were 11 survivors, while as many as 21 died due to drowning and exposure. Two have been arrested by Albanian authorities for [[people smuggling]], while other senior officials have been implicated in connection with the tragedy.<ref>{{cite web|last=Willey |first=David |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3386481.stm |title=Europe &#124; Albania mourns smuggled migrants |publisher=BBC News |date=2004-01-11 |accessdate=2015-11-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://edition.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/01/10/albania.immigrant.ap |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070325040112/http://edition.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/01/10/albania.immigrant.ap/ |archive-date=2007-03-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.reuters.co.uk/newsPackageArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=436718&section=news |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041010075010/http://www.reuters.co.uk/newsPackageArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=436718&section=news |archive-date=2004-10-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
